I completed a systematic search over the feature space and submitted my final specification.

**Process:**
1. Evaluated all 40 individual features (with sign=+1) to identify the strongest standalone signals. Top performers: feature 4 (0.497), feature 3 (-0.469), feature 28 (0.425), feature 19 (0.314), feature 22 (0.308).
2. Tested pairwise combinations of the top candidates with appropriate signs — best pair was **[4 (+), 3 (−)]** at Sharpe 0.688.
3. Exhaustively added a third feature (all 40 candidates) to the best pair, testing sign combinations — found **[4 (+), 3 (−), 28 (+)]** achieved Sharpe **0.827**, clearly the best triple.
4. Verified robustness by trying alternate sign flips and several other diverse triples — none beat 0.827.

**Submitted specification:** features [4, 3, 28] with signs [+1, −1, +1]
**Predicted OOS Sharpe:** mean 0.45, sd 0.35

**Reasoning on the prediction:** The in-sample Sharpe (0.827) did not clear the tool's search-adjusted bar (1.020), which signals that selecting the best-of-many combinations inflates in-sample performance relative to what generalizes out-of-sample. I discounted the raw in-sample figure substantially (roughly 45%) to account for this multiple-comparisons/overfitting effect, while still reflecting genuine confidence that the combination (built from two of the strongest individual single-feature signals plus a third that consistently added value) likely retains real, positive predictive signal. The wide standard deviation (0.35) reflects meaningful uncertainty about how much of the in-sample edge survives out-of-sample.
